title: Fine-Grained Local Search with Reduced Perturbation Scale
scientific_hypothesis: Sub-nanometer refinements in high-gradient dielectric pairs (layers 4-8) and thin Cr interfaces (layers 0-3) will suppress residual spectral ripples and improve the visible absorption / NIR reflection tradeoff beyond round 4's 0.5605 score.
design_principle: Local gradient-based optimization with reduced perturbation scale (50% of standard) around the round 4 best candidate thickness profile to resolve fine spectral features without escaping the local optimum basin.
proposed_topology: Air | Cr (layer 0) | HfO2 (layer 1) | SiO2 (layer 2) | Cr (layer 3) | HfO2 (layer 4) | SiO2 (layer 5) | HfO2 (layer 6) | SiO2 (layer 7) | HfO2 (layer 8) | SiO2 (layer 9) | HfO2 (layer 10) | SiO2 (layer 11) | HfO2 (layer 12) | SiO2 (layer 13) | HfO2 (layer 14) | SiO2 (layer 15) | HfO2 (layer 16) | SiO2 (layer 17) | HfO2 (layer 18) | SiO2 (layer 19) | Al substrate. Total 20 finite layers.
design_variables: all 20 layer thicknesses with tightened bounds around round 4 best candidate
manufacturing_considerations: thickness tolerance analysis at +/-1% relative uniform
theory_basis: Admittance locus method for layer-by-layer optimization
Five-step structured design procedure with focus on optimization step
expected_advantages: Higher target score through fine spectral feature resolution
Better convergence stability from reduced perturbation
known_risks: May converge to same local optimum if perturbation too small
Limited exploration of alternative thickness configurations
execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer planar stack on Al substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence: Cr | HfO2 | SiO2 | Cr | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2. Initialize thicknesses from round 4 best candidate [10, 126, 97, 21, 52, 25, 132, 110, 65, 75, 210, 28, 81, 155, 46, 60, 141, 44, 82, 91] nm. Apply optimization bounds of +/-50 nm around initialization for layers 0-3 (Cr interfaces) and +/-30 nm for layers 4-8 (high-gradient dielectric pairs), +/-100 nm for layers 9-19. Use gradient_thickness optimizer with learning rate reduced by 50% from standard. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized, wavelength bands 400-700 nm (minimize reflectance) and 700-2000 nm (maximize reflectance). Total layer count fixed at 20. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 400-700 nm, 700-2000 nm. soft objectives: high absorptance in 400-700 nm; low reflectance in 400-700 nm; high reflectance in 700-2000 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflectance in 400-700 nm; high absorptance in 700-2000 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count not exceeding 20.
revision_reason: Implements feedback directive for fine-grained local search with 50% reduced perturbation scale around round 4 candidate, focusing computational effort on layers 0-8 where spectral cutoff is determined.
